_doc: PRE-REGISTERED cohort/method/pass-bar for the block_elite_bull SS-B revalidation. Frozen BEFORE any replay is run (exploratory != confirmatory -- no re-picks after seeing results; FAIL is publishable). RELAUNCH of the study a PC reboot killed on 2026-07-09; today (2026-07-10) SPY drifted +$3-4 while block_elite_bull blocked 20 more ELITE-tier bull ticks, motivating the re-audit. Runner: backtest/tools/block_elite_bull_ssb_revalidation.py.
account_scope: safe (Gamma-Safe-2) ONLY -- matches the original probe's production config (automation/state/params.json, initial_equity=1763.0). Bold is NOT in scope (different VIX band [15,18), never audited by the original probe; a separate study).
direction: bull (side=C) only -- block_elite_bull never touches bear.

part_a_original_n7.method: run_backtest(use_real_fills=True) A/B: BASE=block_elite_bull True vs UNBLOCK=False, same production Safe config otherwise (strike_offset=-2, per_trade_risk_cap_pct=0.30, initial_equity=1763.0, enable_bullish=True, no_trade_before=09:35). Added cohort = trades present in UNBLOCK but not BASE, filtered side=='C'.
part_a_original_n7.reuse_note: This study RE-RUNS this exact A/B (same _bull_cfg, same window) rather than trusting the saved JSON, so the 7 Trade objects' entry_time_et/strike/entry_premium/rejection_level are available in-memory for the SS-B replay. The re-run's added-cohort net_pnl vs -241.26 IS the old-exit parity check (condition 3 of the pass bar).

part_b_extension.note_window_boundary: Starts 07-01, not 06-30, because 06-30 is already fully covered by part_a via the full-backtest re-run (avoids double-counting the same calendar day through two different mining methods).

super_comparison_cohort.filter: tier derivation per backtest/lib/engine/engine_cli.py:481-484 _derive_tier: (confluence AND ribbon_flip in triggers) OR len(triggers)>=3 => SUPER. block_elite_bull structurally never blocks SUPER (gates.py:271 checks tier=='ELITE' only) -- this is the natural comparison group: what would SS-B do to the population the gate under test never touches, over the identical window.
super_comparison_cohort.role: SECONDARY / DISCLOSURE ONLY -- NOT gated by its own pass bar. Reported alongside the elite cohort for context, per the mission's 'natural comparison group' instruction.
super_comparison_cohort.known_thin_n_disclosure: Raw-tick scan (done at freeze time to size this cohort) found only 22 raw ticks / ~4-6 deduped events across the full 51-day window on safe -- this cohort will almost certainly land under the elite cohort's own n>=12 floor. Its role is qualitative comparison, not a second pass/fail gate.

dedupe_rule.statement: Sort a cohort's matching decision-log rows by ts_et. The FIRST row starts event 1. Each subsequent row joins the CURRENT event if the gap since the previous row's ts_et is <= 5 minutes; a gap > 5 minutes starts a NEW event. An event's entry_time_et/spy_spot/trigger_level_exact are taken from its FIRST row (the earliest actionable tick).
dedupe_rule.rationale: 5 minutes anchors to this codebase's native SPY/ribbon bar granularity (every gate, filter, and level check in this engine operates on 5-min bars) rather than an arbitrary round number. It is also the shortest realistic 'still evaluating the same setup' gap given the heartbeat's ~1/min tick cadence -- shorter gaps are jitter/normal re-evaluation of an unchanged setup, longer gaps mean the setup condition genuinely cleared and later re-armed.
dedupe_rule.sensitivity_disclosure: The revalidation output additionally reports event counts at 2-minute and 15-minute thresholds so the n>=12 pass-bar check is not silently threshold-dependent.

stale_echo_exclusion.problem: backtest/lib/engine/gates.py's evaluate_gates() runs INSIDE engine_cli.decide_payload, which executes BEFORE heartbeat_core.py's post-verdict ladder (_past_entry_ceiling / _stale_trigger_bar / _before_entry_floor, heartbeat_core.py:827-847). That ladder only runs when the raw verdict is ENTER_BEAR/ENTER_BULL. So when a stale bar carried over from the PRIOR session (the '2nd-to-last fetched bar is yesterday's 15:50/15:55 close' edge case _stale_trigger_bar's own docstring names) triggers a GATE_ORDER block INSIDE decide_payload before ever reaching a raw ENTER verdict, the stale-trigger-bar guard never runs and the row is logged under the GATE's name, not SKIP_STALE_TRIGGER -- a mislabeled phantom signal. CONFIRMED live on 2026-07-10: bold's 5x SKIP_CONF_LVL_REC_AFTERNOON at 09:31-09:35 ET fired on the SAME stale prior-day (2026-07-09 15:55 ET) trigger bar that safe's SKIP_STALE_TRIGGER independently caught at the identical timestamps (see the Part-1 audit, markdown/audits/ this session's report).
stale_echo_exclusion.exclusion_rule: A candidate event is EXCLUDED from the primary cohort if its first-tick timestamp has a same-second-or-near (+/-90s) row on the OTHER account (bold) whose action == 'SKIP_STALE_TRIGGER' at that instant -- direct cross-account corroboration that the underlying bar was a prior-session echo, not a live signal.
stale_echo_exclusion.flag_only_rule: A candidate event whose first tick lands within 09:35:00-09:41:00 ET (the documented at-open stale-bar-carryover risk window) but has NO cross-account corroboration is FLAGGED (elevated_stale_risk=true) but NOT excluded -- disclosed, not silently dropped. The revalidation output reports the pass-bar verdict both with and without flagged events included.

strike_convention.rule: backtest/lib/simulator_real.py:372-376 (the production/original-probe convention, strike_offset=-2 from _bull_cfg): atm = round(entry_spot); for side=='C', strike = atm + strike_offset = atm - 2 (ITM by $2).
strike_convention.sim_accuracy_check_OP16: This is DELIBERATELY NOT the same convention as backtest/tools/t4_exit_matrix.py's _load_bars (strike = round(spot) + 2 for calls, OTM by $2) used by structure_stop_study.py's layer (a)/fresh-slice signals. The two tools encode OPPOSITE strike conventions under the same '-2' label. This study uses the simulator_real/_bull_cfg convention throughout (both the re-run part_a AND the newly-mined part_b/comparison events) because that is what actually produced the -$241.26 the parity check must reproduce, and it is what the original bull_unblock_replay_probe.py -- the artifact this whole study is extending -- used. Verified against current production: automation/state/params.json v15_strike_offset_per_tier lists strike_offset=-2 for the $2-10K equity band; Safe-2 equity ($1,763 at last mark) sits at the boundary of the $1K/-3 and $2-10K/-2 tiers -- the original probe hardcoded -2 regardless, and this study reuses that exact choice for cohort continuity rather than re-deriving a tier that could silently change the signal definition mid-study.
strike_convention.atm_rounding: round(spot) to nearest whole dollar, matching simulator_real._strike_from_spot.

entry_premium_recovery.part_a_original_n7: Read directly off the re-run's Trade objects (t.entry_premium, t.entry_time_et, t.rejection_level) -- the same real-OPRA-fill values the original probe's simulator computed, no separate recovery needed.
entry_premium_recovery.part_b_and_comparison: Real Alpaca OPRA option bars via backtest/tools/exit_shape_parity_study.fetch_option_bars(symbol, date_et) [1-min bars], tried first against the local cache (backtest/lib/option_pricing_real.load_contract_bars) to avoid redundant network calls, falling back to a live fetch (OPRA reads are $0 / free this session per the mission). entry_premium = the OPEN of the first available 1-min option bar with timestamp_et >= the event's entry_time_et (no look-ahead: the earliest tradeable print at or after the signal tick). A signal whose option bars cannot be recovered (illiquid strike / API gap) is DROPPED and counted in n_missing_bars, never silently imputed.

trigger_level_recovery.rule: Use the decision-log's own trigger_level_exact field when present (only populated on rows from ~2026-07-10 11:51 ET onward -- a recent logging addition). For rows before that (all of part_b's 07-01..07-09 span), recover it via backtest/tools/tw8_level_context.py's frozen_level_set_for_date + lib.filters.detect_level_reclaim against that day's SPY 5m bars -- IDENTICAL detector to the one the live engine itself used to fire the signal, applied at the event's own entry bar. This is the exact-match method (not the backward-scan heuristic structure_stop_study.py uses for real fills with no entry_spot label), because the decision log DOES give an exact entry spot/time.
trigger_level_recovery.fallback: If no level in the day's frozen set reclaims at the entry bar (should not happen given the row was logged with triggers containing level_reclaim, but disclosed as a defensive fallback), the event falls back to premium-only (-50% catastrophe cap only, no structure layer) for its SS-B replay, per the same convention structure_stop_study.py uses for its own fallback population -- never dropped, never faked.

OLD.label: shipped -20%/+150%/sell80/fixed premium-only shape (the exact shape that produced the original -$241.26)

SS-B.label: structure stop (5m SPY close back below the reclaimed level) + -50% catastrophe cap + TP1 +100% sell66 + runner trail 15%
SS-B.source: backtest/tools/structure_stop_study.py SS_B_SHAPE (the exact frozen SS-B cell from the 2026-07-09 structure-stop-preregistration.json, reused verbatim)
SS-B.c6_fill_mark_convention: structure stop fires at the NEXT 5m SPY bar's OPEN premium (the earliest tradeable price once the breach is knowable), never the breaching bar's own close -- backtest/tools/structure_stop_study.py structure_stop_signal_time().

exit_shapes.replay_engine: backtest/tools/structure_stop_study.py replay_structure_aware() + structure_stop_signal_time(), reused unmodified. Time stop 15:50 ET (exit_manager.TIME_STOP_ET, the layer-b/exhibit convention, since these are live-decision-log-sourced signals like layer b, not the cached FRESH_SIGNAL_SET like layer a).
exit_shapes.qty_convention: ELITE-tier events replay at qty=10, SUPER-tier comparison events at qty=15 -- backtest/lib/orchestrator.py:1178-1184's own quality-tier sizing table (SUPER=15, ELITE=10), applied identically to both exit shapes so the OLD vs SS-B comparison isn't confounded by a qty difference.

pass_bar.statement: Unblock is PROPOSED (staged, not applied) only if ALL FOUR hold for the elite cohort (part_a re-run + part_b extension combined):
conditions: 2. SS-B cohort total pnl > 0 after dropping the single largest-magnitude WINNING trade (drop-top-1; guards against a one-trade concentration mirage on a small-n cohort)

3. Old-exit parity: the part_a re-run's added-cohort net pnl reproduces the recorded -$241.26 within a $1.00 tolerance (proves the re-run methodology is byte-faithful to the original probe before trusting its SS-B extension)
4. n >= 12 events (elite cohort, part_a + part_b combined, after stale-echo exclusion)
pass_bar.any_condition_failing: verdict = KEEP (block stays armed); no proposal written.
pass_bar.fable_too_good_discipline: If all 4 conditions pass AND the SS-B total looks unusually strong relative to the OLD-exit total on the SAME cohort, the output must name the specific artifact-hunt performed (day-concentration check, single-signal-dominance check, structure-stop-never-fired check) before the proposal is written -- an extraordinary flip from a validated KEEP to a PROPOSE on the same underlying gate is exactly the shape /fable-too-good warns about.

outputs.staged_proposal_if_cleared: analysis/recommendations/block-elite-bull-ssb-unblock-proposal.json (params key + guard test name + revert instructions -- NEVER applied to automation/state/params.json this session)

rail: ANALYSIS ONLY. Touches NO trading-path file (params.json, heartbeat_core.py, gates.py, strategies.py). Read-only against core-decisions.jsonl and live OPRA option-bar reads (network, $0, explicitly cleared this session -- no mass-grind running).
